answer.evidence: The top cap spans rows 1-7. Its width grows from 8 to 12 to 16 and it overhangs the 14-wide body. A light oval highlight sits at rows 2-4. Row 7 is a darker front-edge line (L=71), and row 8 is a very dark outline (L=17) that acts as eave shadow. Below it the green board front runs rows 9-30 (22 rows) with white lettering. The cap is rounded only at its upper edge, so a flat hat reading is possible. The edge line and shadow below it still make it a top surface (evidence a). The object has no side face and is a small standing signboard.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small vertical sign with a dark green rounded cap, a green panel carrying the vertical text 약국, and a dark base. It shows 11 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 6 (bus-shelter), 12 (kiosk) and 20 (vending) for the references. That is above the bus shelter and close to the kiosk. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills of 5x5 or larger, and the lettering and panel edges break up the surface. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, matching the references, so the outline leans toward the material colour (dark green/teal) rather than black. It has about 4 visible shading steps on the body and cap, slightly fewer than the roughly 5 on the references, but it is a thin, simple sign and reads as the same family as the kiosk and vending machine. It would sit next to them without looking flatter or more sticker-like.
